definitions.explanation: The movement of troops toward a destination or enemy position. Also used figuratively for determined forward progress.

examples.japanese: {軍|ぐん}は{北|きた}へ{進軍|しんぐん}した。
{悪天候|あくてんこう}の{中|なか}、{兵士|へいし}たちは{進軍|しんぐん}を{続|つづ}けた。
examples.english: The soldiers continued their march through bad weather.

examples.japanese: {敵|てき}の{激|はげ}しい{抵抗|ていこう}に{遭|あ}いながらも、{進軍|しんぐん}の{速度|そくど}を{緩|ゆる}めなかった。
examples.english: Despite encountering fierce enemy resistance, they did not slow the pace of their advance.

notes:
USAGE:
Primarily a military term, but sometimes used figuratively for determined progress in business or competitions. The well-known military song {軍艦|ぐんかん}{行進曲|こうしんきょく} is sometimes colloquially called {進軍|しんぐん}ラッパ.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {進軍|しんぐん}する (to advance, to march)
- {進軍|しんぐん}を{続|つづ}ける (to continue the advance)
- {進軍|しんぐん}{速度|そくど} (pace of advance)
- {進軍|しんぐん}ラッパ (bugle call to advance)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {行軍|こうぐん}: march — focuses on the act of marching rather than advancing toward an enemy
- {侵攻|しんこう}: invasion — advancing into enemy territory
